PHASE 2 GATE DECIDED BY ANDREY (round-107, live evidence: 135-file normalization walls on every merge, runtime churn rewriting plan structure under his hands — verbatim: 'я их мерджу, оно постоянно что-то меняется, вся структура, все файлы'). DECISION = OPTION B: the daemon's plan runtime writes MOVE OUT of the git worktree into ~/.codeterm state (per-project plan store keyed by project path); the repo receives plan state ONLY via explicit 'codeterm plan export' (reviewed snapshot commits on demand — history-in-git preserved as a deliberate act, never as churn). Scope: all continuous writers (strides, status, sidecar markdown, INDEX, plan.json) relocate; the watcher watches the state dir; existing in-repo plan history stays as-is (frozen archive — do not delete); a one-time migration imports current .codeterm/plans into the state store; after migration, .codeterm/plans gets a README pointing at export. Priority: FIRST POST-RELEASE LANE — it is actively hostile to the user's daily git workflow. Sequencing note: not before the release (storage rewiring during endgame is forbidden by the same logic as stable-ids).

ROOT CAUSE NAMED + DESIGN REQUIREMENTS for the Option-B lane (round-108, Andrey demanded the exact mechanism; verified in released code): PlanStore::save() runs on EVERY mutation (stride, heartbeat, status flip) and write_atomic -> persist_bodies(plan) UNCONDITIONALLY rewrites goal + every section + every task markdown (body_files.rs:124, write_markdown_atomic:702 — no content comparison). Rewrites are usually byte-identical (invisible), but any serializer evolution (current trigger: normalize_markdown_eof adding the '---'/EOF normalization from the storage lanes) makes the first touch re-emit EVERY file -> the 135-file walls. ALSO A PERF BUG: ~250 temp+rename ops per heartbeat on a 248-task plan — this is the rename/open/stat syscall cluster from the round-85 CPU profile. THEREFORE the Option-B state store MUST be built with: (1) WRITE-IF-CHANGED — read-compare-skip in the markdown writer (kills identical rewrites and the IO storm; cheap, could even land as a standalone pre-fix if a lull allows); (2) PER-ENTITY PERSISTENCE — a mutation persists the mutated entity + plan.json only, never whole-plan fan-out; (3) EXPLICIT MIGRATIONS — intentional serializer format changes run as a one-shot migration wave with a single commit/log entry, never lazily on first touch. These three are acceptance criteria for the relocation lane, not suggestions — relocating the same fan-out into ~/.codeterm would hide the git noise while keeping the IO storm.
